requirement:
`Sources::search_text` returns the matching lines and excerpts in `matches`. The
[`SearchResults`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.search.SearchResults) field
`complete` says whether the result includes every match in scope.

```rust,ignore
pub type TextMatches = SearchResults<TextMatch>;
```
rationale:
The text has three obligations: (1) `Sources::search_text` returns matching lines and excerpts in `matches`. (2) `complete` says whether every match in scope is included. (3) `TextMatches` is the alias `SearchResults<TextMatch>`.

(1) Matches and excerpts. `tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[scoped_text_results_keep_line_numbers_context_and_completeness]` runs the real `Sources::search_text` over temp files. It asserts match counts, and exact `(path, line, excerpt)` tuples for the scoped query with 1 line of context. Excerpts for 0, 1 and 2 context lines are asserted exactly. `sources/tests.rs#fn[defaults_use_provider_primitives_and_keep_one_parse_snapshot]` asserts the path, line and excerpt of a default provider search.

(2) Completeness. The same integration test asserts `complete` is true for an unlimited search. It is false when `limit(2)` omits a third match and false when `limit(1)` omits one. It is true when the scoped search has exactly 2 in-scope matches and a limit of 2. That last case also shows an out-of-scope match in `two.txt` does not make the result incomplete, and `complete` is judged against the scope. `sources/tests.rs#fn[completeness_is_false_only_when_a_match_is_omitted_and_errors_propagate]` covers limits of None, 2, 1 and 0 against 2 matches. It also checks that limit 0 with no matches stays complete, and that an invalid pattern errors.

(3) Type alias. `tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the exports and their item kinds against rustdoc. The other tests use `.matches` and `.complete` on the returned value. Together they would fail to compile or assert if the return type were not a `SearchResults` of text matches.

I found no counterexample that these tests would accept.
